claims.subject: us-white-house
claims.statement: Executive Order 14110, "Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence", is dated and signed at the White House on 30 October 2023.

time.note: Date of the order as printed; Federal Register publication followed on 1 November 2023.

claims.briefQuestion: On what date was US Executive Order 14110 signed?
claims.qualification: Records the order’s issue only. Its later revocation (fl-us-eo14110-revoked) does not change this record.

evidence.passage: Executive Order 14110 of October 30, 2023
THE WHITE HOUSE, October 30, 2023.

claims.subject: us-office-of-the-federal-register
claims.statement: Executive Order 14110 was published in the Federal Register of Wednesday, 1 November 2023 (Vol. 88, No. 210, beginning at p. 75191), as FR Doc. 2023-24283.

time.note: Filed on 31 October 2023 per the filing line.

claims.qualification: Publication date only; the order states no separate effective date. Executive Order 14110 was revoked by Executive Order 14148 of 20 January 2025 (fl-us-eo14110-revoked).

evidence.passage: Federal Register Vol. 88, No. 210 Wednesday, November 1, 2023

claims.subject: us-eo-14110-2023

object.value: Definition of "dual-use foundation model" (Sec. 3(k))

claims.statement: Section 3(k) of Executive Order 14110 defines a "dual-use foundation model" as an AI model trained on broad data, generally using self-supervision, with at least tens of billions of parameters, applicable across a wide range of contexts, and exhibiting or easily modifiable to exhibit high performance at tasks posing a serious risk to security, national economic security, national public health or safety.
claims.qualification: States the order’s definition; whether any named developer’s model meets it is not recorded. The definition continues with listed examples (CBRN, offensive cyber, evasion of oversight) that are not quoted. Executive Order 14110 was revoked by Executive Order 14148 of 20 January 2025 (fl-us-eo14110-revoked).

evidence.passage: means an AI model that is trained on broad data; generally uses self-supervision; contains at least tens of billions of parameters; is applicable across a wide range of contexts; and that exhibits, or could be easily modified to exhibit, high levels of performance at tasks that pose a serious risk

claims.subject: us-eo-14110-2023

object.value: Reporting duty for developers of potential dual-use foundation models (Sec. 4.2(a)(i))

claims.statement: Section 4.2(a)(i) of Executive Order 14110 directs the Secretary of Commerce, within 90 days and under the Defense Production Act, to require companies developing or demonstrating an intent to develop potential dual-use foundation models to provide the Federal Government, on an ongoing basis, with information on training activities, ownership and protection of model weights, and red-team test results.
claims.qualification: The order directs the Secretary; it does not itself impose the duty on companies. The implementing survey and the proposed rule of September 2024 are recorded separately; no record of company submissions is made. Executive Order 14110 was revoked by Executive Order 14148 of 20 January 2025 (fl-us-eo14110-revoked).

evidence.passage: Within 90 days of the date of this order

Companies developing or demonstrating an intent to develop potential dual-use foundation models to provide the Federal Government, on an ongoing basis, with information, reports, or records regarding the following

claims.subject: us-eo-14110-2023

object.value: Interim technical threshold for the Sec. 4.2(a) reporting requirements (Sec. 4.2(b)(i))

claims.statement: Section 4.2(b)(i) of Executive Order 14110 provides that, until the Secretary of Commerce defines the technical conditions, the Secretary shall require compliance with the reporting requirements for any model trained using more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, or more than 10^23 operations if trained primarily on biological sequence data.
claims.qualification: An interim threshold for reporting, set until the Secretary defines technical conditions; the quote stops before the exponents, which the PDF text layer renders without superscript ("1026", "1023") and which are read from the printed page. Executive Order 14110 was revoked by Executive Order 14148 of 20 January 2025 (fl-us-eo14110-revoked).

evidence.passage: Until such technical conditions are defined, the Secretary shall require compliance with these reporting requirements for: (i) any model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than
evidence.note: Continues: 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, or using primarily biological sequence data and greater than 10^23 operations (superscripts lost in the text layer).

Tuesday, January 28, 2025

claims.subject: us-eo-14148-2025
claims.statement: Section 2 of Executive Order 14148 (20 January 2025) lists Executive Order 14110 of 30 October 2023 among the executive actions it declares "hereby revoked".

time.note: Dated by the revoking order’s signature; publication followed on 28 January 2025.

claims.briefQuestion: Which executive order revoked Executive Order 14110, and on what date was it signed?
claims.qualification: Revocation of the order as an instrument. It does not erase EO 14110’s historical record, and the order does not itself say what happened to actions taken under EO 14110 (EO 14179 directs their review).

evidence.passage: The following executive actions are hereby revoked:
(ggg) Executive Order 14110 of October 30, 2023 (Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence).

claims.subject: us-eo-14179-2025

object.value: Review of actions taken under the revoked EO 14110 (Sec. 5(a))

claims.statement: Section 5(a) of Executive Order 14179 directs named White House officials to review immediately all actions taken pursuant to the revoked Executive Order 14110 and directs agency heads to suspend, revise or rescind, or propose to suspend, revise or rescind, actions identified as inconsistent with the order’s policy.
claims.qualification: A direction to review; the order does not list which actions (for example the BIS reporting proposal or NIST guidance) were suspended, revised or rescinded.

object.value: CAISI evaluation of frontier AI systems in partnership with frontier AI developers
